$comment: THE REQUIRED-CHECK CONTRACT (NEW-2, 2026-08-06). This file is the committed, checkable copy of
the status checks the 'Protect Main' ruleset requires before a pull request may merge
WHY IT EXISTS. The ruleset lives on GitHub, not in the repo, so nothing in a build could see it
and nothing could notice when it stopped matching reality. On 2026-08-06 every open pull request
became unmergeable — the required context 'build' sat at 'Expected — Waiting for status to be
reported' on seven PRs at once — and no check anywhere went red, because a required context that
is never reported produces no failure, only silence. GitHub offers no merge control in that
state, to anyone, so the repository cannot get itself out of it.
ui-audit/required-check-audit.mjs asserts, in the ordinary required build, that every context
named here is (a) actually produced by a job in a workflow that runs on pull_request into main,
and (b) still reported when a pull request changes ONLY documentation — the docs-only renumber
push being exactly the change that wedged those seven PRs.
KEEP THIS IN SYNC WITH THE RULESET. Adding a required check on GitHub without adding it here
leaves it unguarded; adding it here without adding it on GitHub fails the build until one of
the two is corrected. That is the intended friction — it is the only thing standing between a
one-word job rename and a silent repo-wide merge outage.
